title: Sharp Bounds on Soft-Policy Risk in Hierarchical Instrument Models without Positivity
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 (typed) BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR — D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field (target=field).
gap_reasons: The note proves an exact attained identified interval for the finite-stratum, known-degree polynomial HCM subclass, together with a genuinely law-specific binary-treatment contact-multiplicity criterion; it does not establish a comparable explicit criterion for treatment alphabets larger than two.
Practical reach is limited by the latent-unit polynomial restriction, known degree, finite kernel strata, and the absence of inference or an implemented endpoint procedure.

The framing respects these boundaries and does not present the open multivariate contact certificate as established, but those boundaries keep the package below a broadly influential or flagship contribution.
proof_attempt_summary: The D0 graph discharged the coefficient-fiber characterization, attained sharp policy interval, boundary-valid finite-plate approximation, and binary contact criterion; the final D0.5 math and decision panels passed without findings. A finite-law conditional-kernel error and source-positioning defects were repaired before banking. tldr: In the finite-stratum Weinstein--Blei hierarchical instrument model, the observational input is the fixed design \(D_{\mathrm{obs}}=(b,P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{BSRY})\), and the soft-policy risk is characterized exactly by compact coefficient fibers whose collapsed candidate laws match both \(b\) and the complete joint \( (B,S,R,Y) \) law while enforcing probability validity over the entire treatment simplex. The resulting policy interval has attained endpoints whose genuine finite-plate HCM sequences approximate the collapsed mechanism through boundary-valid expected-KL convergence; finite plates are not claimed to match the collapsed observed law exactly. For binary treatment, zero-one contacts contribute derivative rows according to their full multiplicities, giving a necessary-and-sufficient point-identification test that can succeed when ordinary evaluation rank fails. The multivariate analogue is isolated as an open real-algebraic contact problem rather than assumed.
gap: Weinstein and Blei identify the hierarchical-instrument soft-policy law under positivity but do not characterize the law-specific set outside that regime. General range, convex-set, and polynomial-program results do not by themselves establish complete HCM observational equivalence or boundary-valid mechanism convergence.
fill: The project supplies the exact fixed-design fiber, attained sharp endpoints, a finite-plate lift indexed by the same observed treatment-kernel tuple, and a binary contact-multiplicity iff criterion, while treating all generic convex and polynomial tools as inherited.
